Floods Disrupt Power Generation and Transmission in Uruguay

MONTEVIDEO, June 12 – Severe flooding triggered by days of heavy rainfall across central and northern Uruguay has disrupted operations at multiple electric utility sites, causing widespread power generation and transmission challenges, industry officials said Wednesday.

Rising waters on the Río Negro and its tributaries have inundated access roads and submerged critical infrastructure at several hydroelectric plants, including those operated by Usinas y Transmisiones Electricas. The company confirmed that floodwaters reached control rooms at its Paso de los Toros facility late Tuesday, forcing a partial shutdown as technicians worked to safeguard equipment.

“The safety of both our staff and the grid is our priority,” said Mariana Figueroa, spokesperson for Usinas y Transmisiones Electricas. “We are taking every precaution and are in constant coordination with the national grid operator to minimize service interruptions.”

Officials warned that the ongoing floods have also hampered coal deliveries to the San Romero thermal plant, managed by Energía Oriental S.A., as key transport routes remain impassable. Emergency teams are using boats and heavy machinery to clear debris and reinforce embankments, but persistent rainfall is complicating relief efforts.

The Uruguayan Association of Electric Utilities said the situation is affecting nearly a third of the nation’s generation capacity, with intermittent outages reported in several towns and rural areas. “We are closely monitoring reservoir levels and grid stability,” said association president Luis Méndez. “If the rain continues, further disruptions are likely.”

Meteorologists forecast continued heavy rain through the end of the week, raising concerns about additional flooding and prolonged outages. The Ministry of Energy has urged residents to conserve electricity and avoid downed lines.

Usinas y Transmisiones Electricas and other operators said they are preparing contingency plans, including the possible rerouting of transmission lines and the deployment of mobile generators. Figueroa added, “We ask for patience and caution from the public while crews work around the clock to restore normal operations as soon as conditions allow.”
